domain_restrictions: k satisfies 0 <= k and k < n
division is well-defined: n is not 0
x and y are real numbers
the monotonicity condition is only required when both x and y lie in the half-open interval [k/n, (k + 1)/n)
semantic_sketch_json.normalized_claim: Fix an index n (so f_n is fixed). For every integer k with 0 <= k < n, and for all real numbers x and y with k/n <= x <= y < (k + 1)/n, it holds that f_n(y) <= f_n(x).

variables.name: n
variables.role: index of the function f_n; also determines subinterval endpoints via division

variables.name: x
variables.role: left point in the monotonicity comparison within a subinterval

variables.name: y
variables.role: right point in the monotonicity comparison within a subinterval

variables.name: f_n
variables.role: maps real inputs to real outputs; property asserted on each subinterval

statement_nl: For every integer k with 0 <= k < n, the function f_n is nonincreasing on the half-open interval [k/n, (k + 1)/n): whenever x and y are real numbers with k/n <= x <= y < (k + 1)/n, one has f_n(y) <= f_n(x).
